site.name: MAITRI
site.title: Edge-AI Enabled Autonomous Drone System for Real-Time Fault Detection in Solar Energy Infrastructure
site.description: A CQUniversity research project exploring intelligent autonomous inspection, lightweight Edge-AI, explainable AI and cyber-resilient technologies for solar energy infrastructure.

about.title: Intelligent inspection for smarter solar infrastructure.
paragraphs: The research proposes a secure and intelligent autonomous drone-based monitoring system powered by Edge-AI for real-time fault detection in solar energy infrastructure.
The framework brings together drone-based RGB and thermal imaging, lightweight AI models, explainability, hardware-aware optimisation and cyber resilience.

objectives: Develop an autonomous drone-based solar inspection platform using RGB and thermal imaging sensors.
Design computationally efficient models for real-time onboard fault detection and localisation.
Integrate XAI techniques to improve interpretability and trustworthiness of AI-based decisions.
Develop secure communication and resilient AI mechanisms against cyber threats and adversarial manipulation.
Optimise AI inference performance for embedded GPU and FPGA-enabled systems.
Validate the framework using benchmark datasets, simulation environments and real-time drone experimentation.
methodology: Drone RGB and thermal imagery; public solar fault datasets
CNN / YOLO-based lightweight models; fault classification and localisation
NVIDIA Jetson / FPGA implementation and real-time inference
Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, latency and energy efficiency

researchQuestions: How can drone systems be integrated with Edge-AI for real-time solar fault detection?
What lightweight AI models can achieve high accuracy under embedded hardware constraints?
How can explainability improve trust in AI-based solar inspection systems?
How can cyber resilience be improved in autonomous drone systems?
Can real-time onboard inference outperform cloud-based systems in latency and efficiency?
